card.name: Words after reduce or decreased effect
card.fires_on: The small word 'to' or 'the' right after a verb like 'reduce' or 'disrupt ability', or the word 'decreased' after 'associated with', in drug-label sentences about lowered effect or function.

modes.label: reduce the
modes.description: The word 'the' straight after 'reduce' where an effect or efficacy is about to be named.
modes.example: Opioids can reduce<< the>> efficacy of diuretics by inducing the

modes.label: ability to
modes.description: The word 'to' after 'ability' when something is said to be impaired.
modes.example: Atypical antipsychotics may disrupt the body’s ability<< to>> reduce core body temperature.

modes.label: decreased after associated with
modes.description: The word 'decreased' after 'associated with' before a drug effect term.
modes.example: Increased metoprolol plasma levels have been associated with<< decreased>> cardioselectivity.

card.plain: It fires on little words in sentences saying a drug lowers or weakens some effect or body function.
